title: Sanctions Screening Database Corruption — Partial List Serving After Upgrade

content.summary: Following a database schema migration on 2024-06-05, the sanctions screening service served a partial (31%) version of the OFAC SDN list for 52 minutes due to a migration rollback that did not re-seed the new schema with the full dataset.

timeline.event: Planned schema migration begins on sanctions-screening database
Migration encounters index creation timeout; partial rollback triggered
Rollback completes but database contains only the first 31% of SDN entries (seeding was not re-run)
Compliance monitoring alert: SDN entry count below threshold (expected 14,800; found 4,600)
P1 declared; wire-transfer-service suspended pending full list validation
Full SDN list re-seeded; all payment processing resumed

content.root_cause: The migration rollback script was designed to restore schema DDL only, not data. After rollback, the database had the old schema with only partially migrated data. The data seeding step was part of the forward migration path and was not included in the rollback path. This is a known gap identified in INC-2024-005's long-term remediation backlog but not yet addressed.
contributing_factors: Migration rollback script did not include data integrity verification step
SDN entry count check was not part of the post-migration smoke test
Related to INC-2024-005 — repeated pattern of sanctions list integrity issues

immediate: Re-seed full SDN list from authoritative source
Re-screen all 1,240 payments processed during partial-list window
short_term: Add SDN entry count assertion to post-migration smoke test (JIRA COMP-520)
Include data integrity check in all rollback scripts (JIRA COMP-521)
Implement pre- and post-migration SDN count comparison gate (JIRA COMP-522)
long_term: Migrate SDN list to append-only immutable storage with versioned snapshots
Blue-green deployment model for sanctions database migrations
Automated re-screening workflow for payments in degraded-list windows
